nkb 0.1.0 - malicious test data, one shortcut away

Usage:
  nkb <command> [options]

Commands:
  packs             List the packs this build can offer
  show <pack>       Print one pack in full
  emit <pack>       Print a pack's values for a script or a file
  send <pack>       Type one value into the focused field
  lint <file>       Check a pack file against the format rules
  fmt <file>        Rewrite a pack file in canonical shape
  new-pack <name>   Write the skeleton for a new pack

  -h, --help        Show this help and exit with 0
      --version     Print the version and exit with 0

formats.name: json
formats.help: Both forms of every value, and every field. The default, because it is the only one that carries the whole catalogue

formats.name: csv
formats.help: One row per value. Escaped by default, because this catalogue contains values that destroy CSV files

formats.name: lines
formats.help: One value per line. Refuses a value containing a line break by name, rather than splitting it silently

commands.help:
nkb emit - print a pack's values for a script or a file

Usage:
  nkb emit <pack> [--format json|csv|lines] [--escaped|--raw] [--base64]

Values go to standard output. The account of what came out, and any
note about what a format could not carry, go to standard error - so a
redirected file holds values and nothing else.

Formats:
  json     Both forms of every value, and every field. The default,
           because it is the only one that carries the whole catalogue
  csv      One row per value. Escaped by default, because this
           catalogue contains values that destroy CSV files
  lines    One value per line. Refuses a value containing a line
           break by name, rather than splitting it silently

Options:
      --escaped  Print values as a pack file stores them
      --raw      Print values literally
      --base64   Encode values, for channels that damage text
  -h, --help     Show this help and exit with 0

commands.name: send
commands.summary: type one value into the focused field
about: Put one value of a pack into whatever field has the keyboard focus.

The value goes to the focused window, not to standard output. Everything you read here is on standard error. Nothing is sent while Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Win is held on the keyboard: the command waits up to two seconds for them to come up, then refuses. Nothing is sent to a window running with higher privileges than nkb, such as an application started as administrator: the system would drop the keystrokes without a word, so the command refuses and exits with 4. Nothing is sent when the keyboard focus is on a button, a link, a list item or a page that is not editable: keys there act on that control, so the command refuses and exits with 4. Where it cannot tell, it sends. Press Escape to stop a send in progress: nothing more is typed, the command says how much arrived and exits with 4. Escape belongs to the command only while it types - before and after, the key is the application's.

options.help: which value, counting from 1 in the pack's own order (default: 1). The order of values is the order of testing.
seconds to wait first, so you can focus the target (default: 3). Use 0 when something else focuses it.

press Home, Shift+End, Delete first, clearing the current line of the field. Never selects beyond the line, so a multi-line field keeps its other lines. Without this switch the only keys sent are the value's own characters.

commands.help:
nkb send - type one value into the focused field

Usage:
  nkb send <pack> [--index N] [--delay S] [--clear]

Put one value of a pack into whatever field has the keyboard focus.

Options:
  --index N      which value, counting from 1 in the pack's own order
                 (default: 1). The order of values is the order of testing.
  --delay S      seconds to wait first, so you can focus the target
                 (default: 3). Use 0 when something else focuses it.
  --clear        press Home, Shift+End, Delete first, clearing the current
                 line of the field. Never selects beyond the line, so a
                 multi-line field keeps its other lines. Without this switch
                 the only keys sent are the value's own characters.
  -h, --help     Show this help and exit with 0

The value goes to the focused window, not to standard output.

commands.name: fmt
commands.summary: rewrite a pack file in canonical shape
about: Puts the fields of each table in the order the format defines and lines up the equals signs. Comments, blank lines and the order of the values themselves are left exactly as they are - the order of the values is the order a tester meets them.

options.help: Say what would change and write nothing
Show this help and exit with 0

exit_codes.help: the file is in shape, or was put in shape
the file is not TOML, so there was nothing to put in order
there is no pack file to read at that path
formatting would have changed a value, so nothing was written
the file could not be read or written, or standard output could not be written

Usage:

themselves are left exactly as they are - the order of the values is the

Options:

  -h, --help     Show this help and exit with 0

commands.name: new-pack
commands.summary: write the skeleton for a new pack
about: The name becomes both the file name and the pack identifier, so it has to be lower case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter. The file is written in the current folder and never over an existing one.
